summary: A managed PR owns a lane reservation while native state remains open. Valid campaign/chain metadata continues to count even when routine head binding or source eligibility is stale. Rewriting a body can erase the lane marker; a recognized canonical routine branch or damaged lane-comment footprint therefore retains an unresolved reservation and refuses further admission without guessing its campaign/chain. This does not expand the cap to genuine unmanaged feature PRs; ordinary prose mentioning the helper is not a lane-comment footprint. Admission observations retain the full paginated native open population and count beside the managed count, so missing classification cannot be mistaken for an authenticated free slot. Source eligibility and exact-head delivery still require their separate canonical gates. Restoring metadata or closing a PR requires authenticated native readback; an old count is not current slot authority.
title: Keep managed PR reservations separate from source eligibility
